title: App Mode Confusion Maze
oneLiner: A playful onboarding maze helps users decide whether to use chat, work-agent, coding-agent, browser, or scheduled-task mode.
targetUser: Power users and teams overwhelmed by overlapping AI app modes, model gates, subscriptions, and connected-tool choices.
keyUX: Answer scenario cards, route through a mode maze, reveal cost/permission tradeoffs, and end with a shareable mode-choice map.
sourceSignalReferences: S1: Hada: ChatGPT Work expands app/file/browser agents - https://news.hada.io/topic?id=31281
S12: Users ask which AI subscription is actually worth paying for - https://www.reddit.com/r/AI_Agents/comments/1rw5xvh/whats_the_best_ai_to_actually_pay_for_right_now/
twist: Makes product confusion visible as a game instead of another help-center article.
smallGroupFit: AI-heavy teams can use it in onboarding or tool-choice workshops.
spreadTrigger: The mode-choice map is funny and useful enough to share in team chat.
stitchPrompt: Create a responsive playful web app called "App Mode Confusion Maze" for users choosing between chat, work-agent, coding-agent, browser, and scheduled-task modes. Include scenario cards, a mode maze board, cost and quota hints, connected-tool permission gates, wrong-mode failure jokes, recommended mode map, and shareable decision receipt. Design direction: use the playful-experimental profile with crisp game-board navigation, lively but readable colors, tactile choice cards, and funny failure states that still teach the right workflow.
